cards.d: 斗罗大陆 · 三國演義 0.04 → 0.85 · named entities in the final graph
per 1M chars (斗罗大陆) · 三國演義 $4.13 → $0.09 · ~50×
三國演義: 416 → 8 over 8 chapters; promotion uses no LLM
legacy coreference often dropped ids from large components

findings: The current coreference fragments more than it merges. It sends every mention of an exact/edit-distance component to llama-3.3-70b in one prompt (a main character is hundreds of lines with context), and any id the model omits stays an unmerged singleton. 61% of names occurring more than once ended up split over several document entities (斗罗大陆: 1,424 entities for 364 gold entities). Its MUC score over surface forms is 0.10 and 0.00 — below the no-LLM exact-string rule (0.50, 0.14).

Surface-form coreference fixes both failure modes. One call per document lists each distinct name once (identical strings merged deterministically first), so nothing is dropped, and aliases that share no characters are in reach (玄德/劉備, 小三/唐三, 雲長/關羽 — the recall ceiling in issue #25). glm-5.3-flash without contexts reached MUC F1 0.81 / 0.84 at $0.04–0.08 per 1M chars; with contexts it gains on 三國演義 (0.89) but loses on 斗罗大陆 for ~5× the cost.

Model choice dominates again, and differently from extraction. gemma-4-26b, the extraction pick, merges too eagerly here (0.35–0.80); llama, mistral, scout, qwen3-30b and glm-4.7-flash group emotions and places into people. glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4.1-flash and qwen3.8-27b are the reliable tier; gpt-oss is precise but misses most aliases. Gold labels are hand annotations, so unlike the extraction eval no model family is favoured by the labels.

For linking to the knowledge scope, a rule beats every LLM. Once entities carry all their aliases, linking a document entity to the one KB entity sharing an exact alias scores 0.995 / 0.969 F1 with no model call. Every LLM linker — the whole KB in the prompt, top-k retrieval, or only the residual queries — scored lower, because models over-link similar names (a city to the school named after it, 劉勝 to 劉備). Production promotion is now this rule; the LLM pass stays available behind an option.

End to end, the new pipeline makes the knowledge graph connected across chapters. Running the actual app code chapter by chapter on a real schema, the share of gold cross-chapter links recovered went from 6% to 98% (斗罗大陆) and 2% to 78% (三國演義) at 94–97% precision. Names mentioned once in a chapter now get a document entity too; before that change they could not be promoted, and recall stopped at 79% / 64% (F1 0.87 / 0.76). The rest of the 三國演義 gap is mostly aliases coreference does not join within a chapter (京師 → 洛陽, 西都 → 長安, 協 → 劉協) and a few wrong merges (少帝 with 陳留王, 玄德 with 文臺), which promotion then carries across chapters.
The thinking mode was not used in any run.
plateNote: Cost is billed Workers AI neurons per 1M characters of source text. Dashed lines are rules with no LLM (exact-string coreference, exact-alias linking). Linking plates give every strategy the gold document entities and a KB of earlier documents' gold entities with all their aliases, isolating the linking decision; the end-to-end plates run the app's own coreference and promotion and score what lands in the graph.
tableNote: Coreference: MUC over surface forms (P/R/F1) and B³ over mentions. Linking: link precision / recall over documents 2..n, NIL accuracy for entities not seen before. End to end: pairwise cross-document F1 over PERSON/LOCATION/GPE/ORGANIZATION forms, and over every form. Frontier rows are marked on the left edge; hover a strategy for its description.
method:
Corpora. 斗罗大陆: the six chapters in the local library (≈43K chars, 403 surface forms). 三國演義: chapters 1–8 of the Project Gutenberg edition (#23950, traditional script, ≈38K chars, 1,163 surface forms), chunked by the app's chunker. Mentions in both come from the production entity extractor (gemma-4-26b, 4-chunk batches), so resolution runs on realistic, noisy input.

Gold. Hand-assigned entity keys per surface form (distinct text + type in a chapter). A form's key defaults to its text across the corpus; exceptions are annotated — 74 aliases for 三國演義 (courtesy names, single-character references such as 操/卓/紹, 京師 → 洛陽, 赤兔馬 → 赤兔) and 21 for 斗罗大陆, plus chapter-specific overrides (「關」 in chapters 5–6 is the pass, not 關羽). Homonyms within one chapter are not modelled.

Baseline. "legacy" is a frozen copy of the current code (eval/resolution/legacy), run unmodified on a SQLite stand-in for D1. The end-to-end runs use an in-memory database with the app's real migrations.

Limits. Two novels, one annotator. Linking is scored with gold entities; with predicted ones, its errors compound with coreference's, which the end-to-end plates measure. Harness: npm run eval:resolution.
